title: Addressing the Hydrologic Scaling Challenge Using Experimental Hillslopes: 13 Years of Discovery at the Landscape Evolution Observatory (LEO) at Biosphere 2
content:
Abstract

The Landscape Evolution Observatory (LEO) at Biosphere 2 has reached its 13th anniversary since the first experiment in 2013. LEO is a large-scale research infrastructure consisting of three artificial hillslopes with unique measurement capabilities and experimental manipulation. It has been designed as an interdisciplinary community resource for studying the interactions among hydrology, geochemistry, and ecology. In Earth sciences, the hillslope scale marks a crucial scale transition to bring small-scale process understanding of hydrobiogeochemistry to the catchment scale. This commentary reviews the scientific accomplishments at LEO from a hydrologic perspective and places the key findings into the context of scaling. We demonstrate how LEO can be utilized to address the long-standing scaling challenge in hydrology, discuss how LEO has advanced the understanding of viable approaches at larger scales, highlight how other disciplines can leverage these conceptual and technical approaches to inquiry, and invite the scientific community to leverage the extraordinary data sets that have been generated through 13 years of experimentation at LEO.
